player.direction: Grounded, guarded; admissions are quiet rather than grand.

sister_anwen.direction: Practical warmth. Concern for a person before concern for an omen.

rook.direction: Quick, observant, dry; never a comic caricature.

mira.direction: Clear and careful; leave room for uncomfortable admissions.

elna.direction: Private grief, with ordinary unforced speech.

toma.direction: A tired father protecting his sleeping daughter.

edric.direction: Measured authority; courtesy with strain underneath.

halvern.direction: Old exhaustion without theatrical ghost effects.

senn.direction: Clipped discipline that softens when admitting responsibility.

white_hart.direction: Patient and intimate; no echo, pitch shifting or monster filter.

len.direction: A lost soldier, vulnerable beneath repeated orders.

merrow.direction: Efficient bureaucracy, uncomfortably close to ordinary conversation.

vale.direction: Careful, precise; a keeper finally willing to speak.

guard.direction: Working guard, direct rather than threatening.

patrol_guard.direction: Wary witness, unsettled by the orders received.

servant.direction: Tired hospitality with a little remaining warmth.

soldier.direction: Relief after lowering a weapon; no shouted delivery.

nessa.direction: Warm and brisk, practical hospitality; a pause when she accepts care herself.

nera.direction: Clear, dry and self-possessed; voluntary warmth without softening her boundaries.

lines.text: I read the road notice. Three missing.
I will give you the register. I am not agreeing to stand in a rite you threatened me into.
You sent them out carrying something the shrine had erased.
I thought new burial thread would quiet it. Someone bound it again with Vargan wire.
I saw the token on the board. Rook has moved his bedding from the window.
Keep your hand closed if you need to. I recognize the shape through your glove.
Someone alive tried to take it from the pack.
The record leaves with us whatever we do to the machinery.
Good. Now decide how we feed the people who did not choose what was ground here.
Put the sword down far enough that my men can see what surrender looks like.
I was on that road in the war. Young enough to call an order the whole explanation.
I said their houses owed ours. It became an excuse before I stopped needing it.
You can give testimony. You still answer for the people hurt this week.
You cannot tell me about Edric. Your memory ends here.
I wrote that we could not hold. I left out that I never went back.
I will not. The copies establish what happened. Each of you decides whether to offer more.
Break the grain condition before you touch the seal. Otherwise the rite only learns a new way to threaten us.
Yes. The renewal is my choice too. I need households to witness the seal before the grain moves.
Then give me another way to get those carts through. Do not give me a principle and leave before winter.
What matters is whether I returned after asking them to change.
Keep the lane clear. That cart is carrying grain, not reinforcements.
The steward wants every token brought inside. People argue less over a missing thing when no one can show it.
The steward says a seal was broken. I can see why he is frightened.
You may still leave by the gate. The road must carry people as well as orders.
Terms offered to someone hungry do not make a free promise.
I set an extra place when the grain drivers are late. It does not get them here, but it keeps someone expecting them.
The archive lamps answer names cut from the old books. Start with the marks along the shelf. Not every answer has a voice.
We were sent for the painted tokens after the creatures gathered. Two men did not come back.
Did your orders include scratching out their names?
Contain the breach. Bring back every object. The paper did not say what to do when a child's name made the wire shake.
I kept them and let the steward keep people from reading them. I will sign that fact.
Anwen puts three empty cups beside the coat Oren left. Rook waits by the door.
The creatures gathered their belongings. Someone alive bound the token afterward and tried to remove it.
I recognize the old carving. You can give it to me, show the village, or keep it while we make copies.
If you show it, show the people behind it a way to stay safe as well.
A moment, hunter. The man behind that screen cannot reach his water.
The cup is on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.
Thank you for the water. He has stopped trying to stand.
The man behind the screen needs the cup on the step. Leave it on the linen by his hand, if you would.
There. Close enough that he need not ask again.
Was he with the missing cart?
You have kept the account where a living hand can reach it. That is something the old oath would not allow.
The grain condition is broken. No one standing here has to promise you anything to eat.
I remember the gate shut. I remember the road hidden. I remember the soldiers entering. I will not tell you those were one man's act.
The copies survive. I will keep them. Some people said no when I asked them to stand beside me. Their answer stays no.
Then begin with your own hands. Do not fill the empty places with another person's vow.
Make the account public and I will leave its judgment with you. Release me quietly and preserve the record without opening every private memory.
Or carry the unresolved binding yourself. Or destroy me and lose what no copy holds.
Whatever I choose, the order stays in the book. Families still need a road home. Edric still has to answer.
The kitchen is working. There is a route and a dry refuge. We have tried the shifts, not just written them down.
Then there are two more things you may attempt. Share stewardship only with the keepers who still freely offer it. An empty place remains empty until somebody chooses it.
And if we leave?
Carry the people and their human records through the prepared passage. Undo this boundary, and its shelter will not follow. Neither will the complete account I hold.
A rota can fail. A refuge can fail. Neither makes the old choices disappear.
Then choose whose work begins when mine ends.
There are spaces beside the names now. For the next shift, and for anyone who needs to stop.
Who fills a space when somebody leaves?
Someone who offers. We ask. We wait. If nobody can, we write that the work is uncovered.
The Hart did not make the work smaller.
No. It can no longer make one person carry it in silence.
A hinge, a rail, and the kitchen latch. Those are the jobs. Nobody promised the iron would stop wearing out.
The rota leaves a gap for weather. Sensible. Weather has never signed anything I gave it.
And if a keeper withdraws?
We close the unsafe part until somebody can do it. A promise is not a brace.
Your shift is still on the board. Unless you have something to tell the board.
The passage is open. The watch still changes at the posted hour.
Some people stayed. Some went on. Their shares were packed either way.
Do the keepers agree about everything?
They agree about the next handover. Tomorrow we may have to talk again.
Then we keep the empty places visible.
And we ask before writing a name in one.
The orders, the signatures and the accounts we recovered are packed. These are human records. They remain evidence.
What is missing?
What only the Hart remembered. We cannot fill that absence by guessing.
Leave the notice where someone returning can find it.
A road to the record. Not a claim that we carried everything.
Dry tools underneath. Sleeping cloths on top. Nobody should have to unpack a whole cart to lie down.
I would prefer a lighter future. This one has cooking pots.
What stays?
The walls. What we cannot carry. The people who freely chose another road know where we are going.
The pots have arrived. Tomorrow somebody still has to cook.
The refuge has beds. It has no oath around it. We keep watch with people now.
Can the road remain open behind us?
While we maintain it. Whoever comes later deserves to know both where it goes and what it costs.
And the Hart?
We chose to leave its shelter and its full account. Keep the copies dry. Do not call them the whole of what we lost.
Count the portions, not the mouths into debts. A person can eat here and still disagree with us afterward.
People keep bringing me empty bowls as if I can fill them with a speech. Give me a table that stays upright. I can begin there.
A common fire saves wood. Carrying shares home saves arguments. I can tell you what either costs; I cannot tell every household which cost to bear.
A beam can look straight and still have a rotten seat. Hold it while I check the bearing. We are building for the cart after ours, too.
The water is slow here until the mill lets a pulse through. Read the wet marks on both banks before you promise anyone a quick crossing.
Mark where a load can wait safely. A route is not open just because someone brave enough can get through it.
A bed should not become another confessional. Let the person sleep first. If they want to tell us anything tomorrow, tomorrow has room for it.
Keep the dressings where a stranger can find them. If only I know where they are, we have built a room that stops working whenever I am tired.

These are two different shelves. The public account belongs where anyone can compare it. A private statement stays sealed under its owner's terms. Do not let the shelves teach us to forget the difference.
I used to call an empty column an administrative problem. Sometimes it means no one agreed to do the work. That is a fact the book must preserve.
If the rota has a gap, put the gap on the board. Hiding it only means the same tired person fills it again.
A handover needs an answer from the next pair of hands. Leaving a bundle beside someone is not the same thing.
I have spent half my life learning which doors want payment before they open. Leave this one easy to find from the road.
These bunks come apart with common pegs. A room that cannot be repaired by the people using it is only waiting to close.
Leave a place by the door for anyone who cannot sleep among strangers yet. They are still staying with us.
The next meal will use what we kept dry today. That is a small promise, but it is one I can check with my own hands.
I can account for the authority I used. I cannot lend you the consent of anyone who once answered to it. Put my answer beside the others, not above them.
That bell is a warning, not a muster. If I answer it, I will come because I chose a watch. Keep my old rank off the board.
The rota shows what is covered and what is vacant. We ask before we put a name in either place.
The rota shows what is covered and what is vacant. We ask before we put a name in either place.
The households reached Hearthward. There's no ward there, or here now. We have the copies; the rest of the Hart's memory is gone.
The households reached Hearthward. There's no ward there, or here now. We have the copies; the rest of the Hart's memory is gone.
I can take the dawn round. If I cannot keep it, I will tell the next keeper. That is what I am offering.
Not another promise today. The beds are still open; my answer need not close them.
I need to leave the dawn round. Put my place back on the board, without putting another name in it.
Will you take a care shift, with the right to step away?
I will take the evening round, and teach someone willing to cover it. No one learns by being volunteered.
I can help with this room. I cannot promise a standing shift.
I cannot carry the evening round now. The medicines and instructions stay here.
Would you choose to share the care work?
One crossing round in the morning. Weather can stop it, and I can leave it. Write both beside my name.
I can explain the route. I am not agreeing to keep it every day.
Take me off the crossing rota. Leave the route marks for whoever comes next.
Will you keep a route shift under these terms?
I will keep the kitchen's count for now. If I stop, the bowls do not stop with me.
I have already promised today's meal. That is all I can give you now.
Someone else must keep the count after today. Nobody loses their share because I am tired.
Would you take a share of the food and delivery rota?
I will check one public copy and protect what was entrusted to me. A record is evidence. It is never somebody's consent.
I can finish these shelves. I cannot become their permanent keeper.
I am leaving this copy with the agreed custodian. The sealed accounts remain under their owners' terms.
Will you keep a copy without claiming its people's choices?
A weekly comparison and an open handover. If I withdraw, the book will show the vacancy. I will not fill it with an order.
I owe you an account of what I administered. That debt is not a promise to take this office.
Mark my shift vacant. The records stay available, and the reasons for my old orders stay in them.
Will you take a record shift with a public handover?
I will move to the refuge. The shrine's record comes with me; the old stones do not.
I will remain with the people who stay. Do not put my name on the departure list.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
If the old shelter is dismantled, do you want to make Hearthward your home?
I will take my own practice to Hearthward. My patients decide for themselves where they go.
I will keep treating people here. Their need for care is not permission to move them.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I choose Hearthward. The copies need a dry place, and I want to live beyond this archive.
I will stay with the archive. You can carry the agreed copies without claiming that I have left.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will move and keep the refuge's accounts. That is my answer, not an order for the staff.
I will stay to account for what remains. Record the households who leave without adding me.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I choose the refuge. I can take my pots and begin another kitchen.
I will keep a kitchen for the people who remain. A meal here will not require their promise to stay.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will make Hearthward my next home. I am choosing this road now; the abandoned escort is still on the record.
I will lead my own next journey. The households' passage does not appoint me to follow them.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will move. I am taking Harl's bell because I choose to, not because the refuge requires a name.
I choose to stay. You may record the loss of the old ward without deciding where my grief belongs.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will move my own belongings to Hearthward. My family's separate choices are not mine to sign.
I will remain at the fold. I understand that the old shelter will be gone.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will move my tools to Hearthward. I can build another hearth; I cannot bring the old protection with us.
I will stay at this forge. The people remaining will still need repairs.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will take my bag to Hearthward. I have left places before; this time the list will tell the truth about it.
I will stay. Keep the route open, but do not mistake knowing a road for agreeing to take it.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will go to Hearthward. The command record travels under its existing custody; this does not put me in charge of it.
I will remain to answer here. Neither departure nor my title changes the record.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
I will go to Hearthward as a witness, without a command. The signed account remains what I did.
I will remain. The account is signed; you do not need to move me to preserve it.
Take my name off the departure list. I am not agreeing to move.
What do you do when nobody needs you?
I usually discover that the linen needs me. It is very persuasive linen.
And if I hid the basket?
I'd sit outside. There is a patch of afternoon sun beside the wall.
Do you want company?
For five minutes. You may tell me something that doesn't require an answer.
Does anyone ever refuse your help?
Nessa has forbidden me to season the stew. She was quite firm.
How bad was it?
People were very thirsty. I thought that was encouraging at first.
Have you tried again?
I chop onions now. Nessa tastes it, and I try to leave the spoon alone.
Do you always explain why you lost?
Only when the explanation is more interesting than the game.
And when it isn't?
Then I improve it. The light is usually at fault.
You could just say I played well.
You played well. There. An exhausting afternoon's honesty. Shall we have another?
Do you ever run out of things to say?
Frequently. I keep three old stories ready so nobody notices.
I notice the one about the shortcut.
Everyone notices that one. It's still quicker than admitting I'm tired.
You can be tired here.
Good. Sit where you can watch the door. I would like to stop doing it for a little while.
Are all the flowers you keep useful?
The yellow ones are dreadful medicine. Very cheerful, though.
You planted them for the color?
Yes. Toma calls them weeds with ambition. I like them better for it.
Will they stay?
As long as they leave room for the roots I need. I can want two things in one garden.
What do you read when the weather keeps you indoors?
Travel accounts. Especially the ones written by people who plainly got lost.
For the descriptions?
For the corrections. You can hear them getting less certain as the pages go on.
Would you make the journeys yourself?
One or two. Somewhere with a warm room at the end, preferably. I'm quite adventurous about warm rooms.
Have you ever made something just because you liked its shape?
A little iron bird. Very poor at being a hook.
Was it meant to be a hook?
That is what I told people. It was meant to be a bird.
Do you still have it?
Somewhere safe. I might try another. The wings were better than the feet.
Are you a patient teacher?
Until somebody picks up the tool. Then my hands start reaching for it.
That sounds familiar.
I know exactly where their thumb should go. Saying it is harder than moving it.
How do you stop yourself?
Hands behind my back. If you see me standing like an officer, somebody is learning something.
What would you change about your room?
Something blue. I haven't decided what. Everyone asks what size I need before asking what I like.
What sort of blue?
Dark enough to look green when the light goes. I saw it once on a traveler's sleeve.
You remembered the sleeve.
I remembered wanting it. That surprised me more.
What makes a good visitor?
One who moves the basket before sitting down. You are improving.
Anything else?
Ask an ordinary question sometimes. What I ate. Whether the roof kept the rain out.
What did you eat?
Bread with too much butter. I enjoyed every bit. You may look less worried now.
Does your daughter take your advice?
She listens closely, which fooled me for quite a while.
Then does what she intended?
Sometimes she tries it my way first. I almost find that worse when hers works better.
Do you tell her?
Eventually. She has learned to wait with a very patient expression. I wonder where she got it.
How do you know when the day's work is finished?
I don't. Usually somebody starts supper without me.
Does the work suffer if you stop?
Most of it waits perfectly well. I come back and find it exactly as annoying as before.
Then why stay?
I like going indoors with an answer ready. Sometimes I ought to go indoors with muddy boots and no answer.
You nearly gave that as an order.
I heard it too. The first word came out before I had chosen the rest.
What were you trying to ask?
Whether there was room for me at the bench. I made it sound like an inspection.
You could try the question again.
Would there be room? You needn't answer quickly. I am trying to remember that part.
You were tapping out a tune.
An old marching song. I cannot remember the second verse.
Did you ever know it?
Probably not. We all sang the first verse louder and trusted the man beside us.
Does that bother you now?
Sometimes. Today I would simply like to remember whether it was about rain or a missing boot.
Have you ever made your own breakfast?
That question has more accusation in it than the last three about the stores.
I was wondering about the eggs.
I can boil an egg. I have been assured that this is not a sufficient household qualification.
Who assured you?
Several people, independently. It appears to be the one matter on which the household agrees.
Do you play an instrument?
Badly enough that people once praised the attempt rather than the result.
Did you believe them?
At first. Then somebody who had not seen me laughed outside the door.
Did you keep playing?
In private. I would rather have learned to hear the wrong note sooner.
Do you write anything for yourself?
Descriptions of weather, lately. They are all much too long.
Let me hear one.
No. I would begin correcting it as soon as you listened, and it would become work.
Then I won't ask again.
You may ask whether I wrote today. That is a different question.
You have ink on your sleeve.
Yes. I was drawing something in the margin and leaned across it.
What were you drawing?
A bird. It has too many feet. I kept starting the feet again.
Will you scrape it off?
I think I'll keep it. It is unmistakably mine.
Does your tea always go cold?
It is usually the first thing I prepare and the last thing I remember.
I can wait while you drink it.
That is unexpectedly difficult to accept. I keep wanting to find you something to read.
I am comfortable waiting.
Then I shall try being comfortable drinking. A moment, please.
Do you take the shortest way home?
Through the service passage. Except when I take the garden gate, which adds seven minutes.
You have timed it?
Once. Then several more times to make sure I wasn't hurrying.
What is worth the seven minutes?
The sound changes outside the walls. I like arriving home after I have stopped hearing the office.
What do you make when you aren't baking?
Small animals from scrap wood. Rook says they are all potatoes with ears.
Is he right?
About the horse. The badger is very good. I refuse to hear otherwise.
Who gets them?
Whoever asks nicely. I keep the badger. An artist is allowed one satisfied customer.
Do you ever eat at someone else's table?
I try. Then I see how they have stacked the bowls and start rearranging them.
What if they ask you to sit down?
I sit. I notice the bowls from there as well.
Perhaps they want your company.
That is what Elna said. Quite sharply, in fact. I had a lovely evening once I believed her.
Where would you go with an empty cart?
Somewhere I had never been asked to take a cart. A difficult destination to put on a map.
Sea or hills?
Hills. I would like to reach the top and have nothing to unload.
Have you chosen a route?
I'm keeping that part for myself a while. Planning it has been pleasant.
What do your crew argue about when the road is easy?
Where to put a wet cup. It is an argument of surprising endurance.
Where do you put yours?
On top of whatever is least likely to fall. Apparently that is not a system.
Do you settle it as their leader?
They have put a small cloth beside my seat. I have decided to regard it as a treaty.
Mind the hot side. A loaf looks much the same before it burns your hand.
The one I told you to mind. There is water by the care bench, if Anwen needs a hand.
The cups are identical.
And a finish to the shift?
These tools are for the new work, then.
Stand on the pale stone. Not because it is lucky. Because it is firm.
Only the ones I want to reach the other side. So far, everyone.
If that is another wager, carry the water first.
The kettle stays here this time.
Your left or the wagon's?
No daylight through the cover.
Heavy end down first. No, the other heavy end. They never put a light one on these carts.
With the wheel, yes. Not with finding advice. I have enough of that.
Last one on firm ground. I counted people before crates this time too.
You did. That was the job, and it is finished. Help me dry the rope before we discuss the next one.
You can count the shares. I'll cut them.
From your thumb on the scale. Sit down, Rook. There is a share for you too.
Then I can count what stays dry, not what the rain leaves me.
The kitchen needs the answer before tomorrow, not a number to wait behind.
Then put the hungry people on the page too.
I intend to. And I'll bring the empty bowls back before you close the book.
I need a rack that doesn't leave the bottom sack in the wet.
I have asked. He says the ground needs an opinion too.
We moved the sound boards off the damp. That much we can do today.
Still work, not a promise you have to make for us.
The rebuilding account reached us. I can plan the next load around what is actually there.
No. Something useful, with its costs written down.
Walk the dry approach with me. We check before anyone steps onto the crossing.
Feel for the loose turn. No load on it yet.
Good. Now it is a checked rope, not a brave prediction.
The tune can finish before the washing starts.
I haven't mentioned the second bucket.
I was about to find another job. You caught me.
I can leave if you want the quiet.
Stay. Tell me the least important thing you saw on the road.
A crow trying to carry a twig through a gap too narrow for it.
Did it turn the twig?
Eventually. It seemed annoyed that this worked.
There was a splendid ending to this story. I put it somewhere between the second inn and the third.
Start with the ending you have.
A man bought a hat. No, the hat was important earlier.
Perhaps he was pleased with it.
You have reduced a triumph of storytelling to a satisfactory purchase.
I am pleased for him.
Yellow, I think. I am allowed to change my mind before you answer.
What are we choosing?
The color I would paint a door if I had a free afternoon.
Yellow would be easy to find in the rain.
That is useful, but I was enjoying how cheerful it would look.
Then yellow. Cheerful first.
Tell me where you would put your thumb. I'll keep my hands here.
Away from the head of the tool.
Good. And your other hand?
Clear of where it comes down.
There. I managed an entire lesson without grabbing anything.
You moved your elbow twice.
Go on. You have the expression you get before a careful question.
Would you rather have a sunny room or a cool one?
Sunny. I can always open a window. That was a good question.
I had two more prepared.
Save them. We can manage a conversation without provisions for the whole week.
Sunny, then.
Do you think it will rain before morning?
I was going to ask you.
That is inconvenient. I had hoped to borrow your certainty.
We could look again before we leave.
Or admit we don't know and get indoors while it is dry.
I prefer that answer.
Move over. I mean—would you mind moving over?
There is room here.
I heard myself. You needn't pretend the first part was courteous.
You asked again.
It takes longer than I expected.
We have time for a question.
I tried practicing with the door open once. Nobody came nearer.
That is a review of sorts.
An unusually unanimous one. I had to laugh before I could close the door.
Did it help the playing?
Not at all. It helped the practice.
Then you had an audience after all.
I wrote three lines this morning and crossed out two.
Are you keeping the third?
For now. It sounds rather pleased with itself.
Must you correct that too?
Perhaps tomorrow. I wanted to tell somebody I had written it.
I am glad you told me.
I have nearly said 'while you wait' three times. You aren't waiting for anything, are you?
No.
Then I can finish this without finding a form for you.
You can.
That was still warm. I had forgotten it could be.
You might try again tomorrow.
I am trying very hard not to ask whether you've eaten.
I have. You may sit without feeding me.
Good. Now I need something else to say.
Tell me about the badger.
An excellent piece of carving. Slightly round. Fierce in the right light.
I look forward to meeting it.
Nothing needs checking for a moment. I have checked that quite thoroughly.
What happens now?
We stand here without discussing the crossing.
The wind has changed.
So it has. That can be the whole conversation if we like.
I would like that.
Hot side of the tray. Other side of the argument.
The small loaf is not a shortage. It's the one I dropped. There, a trade secret.
Set out another bowl. Worry does less harm with something to do.
Weigh before you divide. Generosity that forgets the last household isn't generous.
No one burned? Then give me room and we'll survive it.
A moment between jobs.
Check the strap before leaning on the cart.
The cart has fewer opinions than the crew. More reliable brakes, too.
You can take the next useful job. That's enough for now.
The load is tied to survive a turn, not to look tidy while standing still.
Keep the approach clear. People need a way through.
A moment between jobs.
I'll split it between the two still working. This short knot is spare; pull the turns apart when you want to learn how it holds.
No one has to give testimony for a meal. Keep the empty delivery sleeve; the names inside are mine to protect.
Nessa has heard that every delayed load went into the old mill. Her own missing delivery does not prove that.
The next batch needs water. Bread takes its time, however loudly people ask for it.
I marked that load already. Check the tag before you move it.
Stop where it is firm. You can ask me from there.
A notch for daylight, a hood for night. Neither replaces looking where you step.
The captain is answering for his orders. I am still checking the crossing.
Senn has gone. The rope still needs checking before anyone crosses.
Removing the captain did not mend a single board. Keep this approach clear.
Read the answer before you bring me another seal.
Leave room for the tray. People still have to eat while the great hall talks.
Hold that wheel, would you? The patient has had enough surprises for one journey.
You can sit here. It is a seat, Kael. We needn't decide anything larger over supper.
I can bake less. I cannot tell a child a smaller loaf is the same size.
There you are. Sit down a moment; I can talk without stopping the bread.
I closed the crossing. I can tell you why. I cannot tell you they all got home.
Firm ground this side. Catch your breath before you tell me what happened.
I know you. You were on our escort. You left at the bend.
I learned to set a wheel after that. We still needed to get somewhere.
No. Follow the work line if you mean to help now. Toma knows where it crosses the old road. Do not tell me what I must want from you.
Light crate to the left. Heavy one stays low. Tor says the frame will hold if someone seats that brace.
There was no one left to do it for us. Mind your fingers.
Outside the load. Nobody proves anything by standing under a falling crate.
All here. People first, then crates.
That is what I asked. It does not change the other road.
Good. Help me get the rope dry.
Keep what I gave you. Not a list of everyone who was there. Some of them do not want you finding them.
Start with your own name, Kael. Mine is not the price of putting it there.
The bread can stay by the gate. I am not ready to sit with you tonight.
Thank you. That is all I asked. The next load leaves when I have chosen the route.
Nessa packed too much bread. She says that is a problem for my judgment, not her baking.
I am still choosing. You needn't wait beside the door until I do.
A seat, then. Nothing larger over supper.
